name: Feather Charm
summary: In Anvilmar, Feather Charms catch a warlock instructor’s eye. Frostmane novices carry these crude trinkets, which hold a faint magical power.

sections.title: Troll Trinkets and Dark Studies
sections.body: Southwest of Anvilmar, Frostmane novices carry feather charms through snowy caverns. Their tribe is known for territorial savagery, yet its young trolls practice primitive spellcraft. The charms hold a faint but unmistakable power. Alamar Grimm, the warlock instructor in Anvilmar, studies this crude trollcraft with interest. He uses the charms to test fledgling warlocks as they seek to bind their first imp.

aliases: where do feather charms come from
faq.answer: Frostmane novices carry the charms in a snowy cave southwest of Anvilmar, in Coldridge Valley.

faq.q: Why does Alamar Grimm want them?
aliases: what does grimm do with them
faq.answer: Alamar Grimm finds the charms’ inherent magic intriguing and unexpected in troll craftsmanship. He tests aspiring warlocks’ physical fortitude and magical potential with them before teaching them to summon an imp.

faq.q: Are the Frostmane trolls adept magic users?
faq.answer: The Frostmane tribe is known as crude and hostile, but its novices practice rudimentary spellcasting. Their feather charms focus that basic magic, showing that even fledgling Frostmane casters harness arcane or shamanistic energies.

faq.q: What do the charms look like?
faq.answer: Frostmane novices make simple talismans from feathers and twine. They carry them as foci for early magical training in Dun Morogh’s cold caves.

angles.text: As a novice warlock in Dun Morogh, you take feather charms from troll spellcasters as a test of discipline. After you pass, Alamar Grimm entrusts you with the ritual to summon an imp.
As a gnome warlock in Anvilmar, you study these rudimentary troll fetishes to examine the raw, unrefined magic channeled by primitive Frostmane casters.
